purpose: hyperparameter selection on validation diseases only; not a final/locked-test result

environment.device_anomaly_note: CUDA was available but every search run used device=cpu -- run_validation_search() never forwarded a device override to its per-config GPUTrainingConfig (default device='cpu'), so the search ran ~6-7x slower than the measured GPU profile would predict. This is an infrastructure/plumbing gap, not a methodology or correctness issue: identical math, slower wall-clock only. Fixed for final training (see repo commit that threads --device through to transe_train_gpu.train_final); the already-completed search itself was left untouched per the scientific-integrity instruction not to rerun or alter it.

search.rule: 1) highest validation MRR; 2) if the absolute MRR difference is <= 0.0005, highest macro AP; 3) if still tied, smaller embedding_dim.
search.triples_used: tuning_triples only (8,097,798 triples; validation and locked-test diseases' indications both absent)

winner.name: search-dim128
winner.selection_reason: highest validation MRR (0.014807 vs. 0.012913 for search-dim64; difference of 0.001894 exceeds the 0.0005 tie-break threshold, so no tie-break was needed)
winner.cross_checked_independently: two independent re-derivations from the raw per-epoch history (one ad hoc, one via the previously-built search_result_lib.py/analyze_search_results.py tooling) both reproduce search-dim128 as the winner and agree with the kernel's own recorded selected_name/selected_index
